insight: The zer- prefix is German's destruction prefix — it signals that something is broken apart completely and irreversibly: zerbrechen (shatter), zerreißen (tear apart), zerschlagen (smash), zerquetschen (crush). Verwirklichen comes from wirklich (real/actual), so literally 'to make real'. Realisieren is the international synonym. Wagen always implies courage against risk — the related noun Wagnis means a risky venture. Zulassen is the administrative verb for permitting or licensing: Zulassung zum Studium (university admission), Fahrzeugzulassung (vehicle registration).

insight: Beispiel, Begriff, and Bedeutung are the three essential vocabulary words of academic and classroom German. Zum Beispiel (z.B.) = for example; zum Begriff werden = to become a household name; von großer Bedeutung = of great importance. Im Begriff sein + infinitive is an extremely common phrase meaning to be just about to do something. Bildung is one of German's most culturally loaded nouns — it spans education, culture, and personal formation. A 'gebildeter Mensch' (a bildung-having person) implies not just schooling but broad cultural awareness. Bibliothek vs. Bücherei: Bibliothek is larger and academic; Bücherei is smaller and local/public.

insight: Übersetzen is one of German's notable homograph pairs. Inseparable überˈsetzen (stress on second syllable) = to translate across languages. Überblick and Einblick and Ausblick form a family of Blick compounds: Überblick = overview (from above), Einblick = insight (looking in), Ausblick = outlook/prospect (looking out). Verständnis is tricky: ich habe Verständnis für = I understand and sympathise with, not simply 'I understand the words'.

insight: Schweigen is the verb for deliberate silence — staying silent when one could speak. The related adjective schweigsam (taciturn) describes a permanent trait (Day 12). Laut is both an adjective (loud) and a preposition taking the dative: laut Gesetz (according to the law), laut Bericht (according to the report) — very common in news writing and official language. Vorlesen is the separable compound: er liest vor (present), er las vor (Präteritum). The related Vorlesung is a university lecture — historically a 'reading before students'. Ruhig softens commands in spoken German: Du kannst ruhig gehen = you may as well go / it is perfectly fine to go.

insight: Sprache vs. Zunge: in German the word for language is Sprache (from sprechen), not Zunge (tongue) — Muttersprache is the mother tongue but the metaphor is speech, not tongue. Wörtlich vs. buchstäblich: both mean literally, but wörtlich refers to word-for-word translation (wörtliche Übersetzung), while buchstäblich (letter by letter) is used for emphasis: Er ist buchstäblich verschwunden = he literally disappeared. Zuhören takes a dative: jemandem zuhören. Anhören takes an accusative: etwas anhören (listen to a piece of music) or is reflexive: Das hört sich gut an (that sounds good). Aussprache has two meanings: pronunciation AND frank discussion (eine Aussprache haben).

insight: Sprechen, reden, and sagen form the core speaking trio. Sprechen is the neutral all-purpose verb for using language — Deutsch sprechen, über ein Thema sprechen. Reden implies more extended, informal, or emotionally coloured talk — Wir müssen reden (we need to talk). Sagen specifies what was said — er sagte, dass... Rufen (call/shout) and its compound anrufen (phone) are essential: Beruf (profession) literally means a calling (from rufen). Stimme covers both voice and vote — the double meaning is transparent in Stimmzettel (ballot paper) and Abstimmung (vote/ballot). Satz has at least four meanings: sentence (grammar), set (tennis), rate (finance: Steuersatz), and a leap (einen Satz machen = to jump).

words.breakdown_note: Talk or speak — more informal or continuous than sprechen. Eine Rede halten = to give a speech. Über etwas reden = to talk about something. Gerüchte/Unsinn reden = to talk nonsense/rumours.

examples.de: Wir haben lange über das Problem geredet.
examples.en: We talked for a long time about the problem.

examples.de: Wir müssen ernsthaft über dieses Problem reden.
examples.en: We need to talk seriously about this problem.

examples.en: We need to talk seriously about this problem.

words.breakdown_note: Call or shout. Rufen Sie einen Arzt! = Call a doctor! Anrufen = to call by phone. Beruf = profession (lit. a calling — from rufen). Um Hilfe rufen = to call for help.

examples.de: Er rief laut nach Hilfe.
examples.en: He shouted loudly for help.

examples.de: Ruf mal an, wenn du ankommst.
examples.en: Give us a call when you arrive.

examples.de: Sie rief seinen Namen, aber er antwortete nicht.
examples.en: She called his name but he did not answer.

examples.de: Sie rief seinen Namen, aber er antwortete nicht.
examples.en: She called his name but he did not answer.

words.breakdown_note: Say or tell — one of the most basic verbs. Ich sage dir = I'm telling you. Sag mal = tell me/say. Das heißt = that means; so zu sagen = so to speak.

examples.de: Was wolltest du mir eigentlich sagen?
examples.en: What did you actually want to tell me?

examples.de: Er sagte, er kommt morgen.
examples.en: He said he would come tomorrow.

examples.de: Ich wollte dir schon lange sagen, wie sehr ich dich schätze.
examples.en: I have wanted to tell you for a long time how much I appreciate you.

examples.de: Ich wollte dir schon lange sagen, wie sehr ich dich schätze.
examples.en: I have wanted to tell you for a long time how much I appreciate you.

words.breakdown_note: At least four meanings: sentence (grammar), leap (einen Satz machen), set (tennis), and rate (Steuersatz = tax rate). Hauptsatz = main clause. Nebensatz = subordinate clause. Satzzeichen = punctuation mark.

examples.de: Bilde einen Satz mit diesem Wort.
examples.en: Form a sentence with this word.

examples.de: Bilde einen Satz mit jedem neuen Vokabular.
examples.en: Form a sentence with each new vocabulary item.

words.breakdown_note: Speak — the standard all-purpose verb for language use. Present: ich spreche, du sprichst, er spricht (e→i). Sprecher = speaker. Compare: reden (informal, extended talking), sagen (say a specific thing).

examples.de: Sie spricht fließend Deutsch und Englisch.
examples.en: She speaks German and English fluently.

examples.de: Können wir nach der Stunde kurz miteinander sprechen?
examples.en: Can we speak briefly with each other after the lesson?

examples.de: Können wir nach der Stunde kurz miteinander sprechen?

words.breakdown_note: Voice or vote. Mit leiser Stimme = in a soft voice. Stimmzettel = ballot paper. Abstimmen = to vote. Seine Stimme abgeben = to cast one's vote. Stimmung = mood (related).

examples.de: Er hat eine sehr angenehme Stimme.
examples.en: He has a very pleasant voice.

examples.de: Bei der Wahl bekam sie die meisten Stimmen.
examples.en: In the election she got the most votes.

examples.de: Bei der Wahl gab sie ihre Stimme für die Grünen ab.
examples.en: In the election she cast her vote for the Greens.
